Camping Trip Checklist

Camping is easy to enjoy and easy to get wrong — a missing tent pole or a bag too thin for a cold night can spoil an otherwise perfect trip. This checklist covers shelter, sleep, food, water, and safety, plus the small things that are miserable to be without. See more travel checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

Camping Trip Checklist · 16 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Reserve your campsite and check its rules on fires, pets, and check-in

    Some sites ban campfires in dry season.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Pack the tent, groundsheet, and enough stakes, and pitch it once at home

    Find missing parts before you're setting up in the dark.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bring sleeping bags rated for the night-time low, plus sleeping pads

    Most of the cold comes up from the ground, so the pad matters as much as the bag.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Pack a camp stove with enough fuel, a lighter, and waterproof matches
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bring cookware, utensils, a sharp knife, and biodegradable soap
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Plan your meals and store food in a sealed cooler or bear-proof container

    Keeps food fresh and wildlife out of camp.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bring plenty of drinking water, plus a filter or purification tablets
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Pack headlamps, a lantern, and spare batteries
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Dress in layers, with rain gear and a warm hat for the evening
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bring sturdy, broken-in footwear and several pairs of dry socks
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Pack a first aid kit, insect repellent, and sunscreen
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Carry a paper map and compass or GPS, and tell someone your plans

    Cell signal is unreliable in the backcountry.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bring trash bags and pack out everything you bring in

    Leave No Trace: the site should look untouched when you go.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Pack a multi-tool, duct tape, and paracord for quick repairs
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Check the forecast and pack for the worst weather it suggests
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bring toilet paper, a trowel, and hand sanitizer

Frequently asked questions

What do I need for my first camping trip? expand_more

The essentials are shelter and sleep (tent, stakes, a sleeping bag rated for the temperature, sleeping pad), cooking (stove, fuel, cookware, water), light (headlamp and spare batteries), and safety (first aid, warm layers, a map). Borrow big-ticket gear for a first trip before you commit to buying.

How do I stay warm while camping? expand_more

Use a sleeping bag rated below the expected low and a sleeping pad to insulate you from the ground, which is where most heat is lost. Dress in dry layers, wear a hat to bed, and eat a warm meal before sleeping. Change into dry socks and base layers at night rather than sleeping in what you wore all day.

What food is easiest to bring camping? expand_more

Foods that don't need refrigeration or much prep: oats, trail mix, pasta, rice, canned beans, tortillas, and hard cheese. Pre-chop and portion ingredients at home to cut cleanup at the site. Keep anything perishable in a cooler with ice, and store all food sealed and away from your tent.
